description:
Redwood Inference is launching a production performance-regression canary focused on serving runtime tail latency and throughput stability. The goal is to detect p95 latency and tokens/sec regressions per model (and per critical configuration slice) early—before they impact customer traffic broadly—then alert the right oncall with enough context to triage quickly.

Scope and goals:
- Deploy a low-footprint canary workload that continuously exercises representative inference patterns (prefill+decode, streaming and non-streaming) for a curated set of models and regions.
- Compute stable time-series for p95 latency and tokens/sec, with guardrails for noise (warmup, sample size, outlier handling) and bias (batching/scheduler effects).
- Trigger alerts when regressions exceed agreed thresholds vs a baseline (e.g., last 7d median or pinned “known-good” runtime build) and automatically attach debug context (runtime version, kernel selection, scheduler mode, GPU type, batch stats).
- Integrate with existing observability stack (metrics, tracing, dashboards), paging via SRE oncall, and a clear runbook for mitigation/rollback.

Non-goals:
- This is not a full customer-facing “perf SLA” product feature in v1; it is internal detection and operational readiness.
- Not a replacement for offline benchmark-lab; instead it complements pre-merge and pre-release suites by catching production-only interactions (fleet heterogeneity, contention, kernel autotune drift, scheduler heuristics under mixed load).

Key stakeholders:
- Serving Runtime (Kernel + Scheduling): owns instrumentation, runtime versioning hooks, and interpreting perf regressions (Mateo Alvarez, Sofia Ivanova, Hiro Tanaka, Noah Patel, Omar El-Sayed).
- SRE/Infra: owns alerting policy, paging hygiene, and incident response integration (Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Allison Grant).
- Telemetry/Observability: owns metrics definitions, aggregation/cardinality controls, and dashboards (Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman, Caleb Johnson).
- Product (Console & Rollouts): ensures alignment with rollout/canary standards and future externalization of perf regression signals (Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes).

Phases and timeline (target ~8 weeks):
1) Requirements + metric definitions (week 1–2): choose models/slices, define latency and tokens/sec computations, select baseline strategy, set initial thresholds.
2) Canary service + instrumentation (week 2–4): implement runner, config, tagging, runtime version capture, and minimal overhead scheduling.
3) Dashboards + alerting + runbooks (week 4–6): build per-model/regional views, regression detectors, alert routing, and standardized triage steps.
4) Safe rollout (week 6–8): start in one region + limited models, tune noise/thresholds, add automated links to recent runtime deploys/PRs, then expand coverage.

Constraints and risks:
- Cardinality and aggregation cost: per-model metrics can explode; must standardize labels and aggregate carefully.
- Fleet heterogeneity: GPU SKU differences must be accounted for or split into explicit slices.
- Canary must be “small and safe”: rate-limited, non-invasive, and isolated from customer SLOs.
- Alert fatigue: regression detectors must avoid paging on known events (deploy windows, cache warmups) and include suppression/maintenance windows.

Deliverables:
- A production canary runner/service with configuration, logging, and safe deployment.
- Metrics spec and implementation for p95 latency and tokens/sec with regression detection.
- Dashboards + alert rules + incident/runbook integration.
- Post-rollout review with threshold tuning and a backlog for v2 improvements (e.g., richer workload mixes, automated bisect hints, model-specific baselines).

files.description: High-level overview page: problem statement, why prod canary is needed vs offline benchmarks, ownership, and current status/coverage (models/regions).
Design doc for the canary system: architecture, workload generator approach, isolation strategy, baseline computation, and how it tags runtime/kernel/scheduler dimensions.
Metrics specification: exact definitions for latency p95, tokens/sec, sample windows, label schema, aggregation, and cardinality controls (with examples).
ADR documenting baseline choice (rolling vs pinned known-good), rationale, trade-offs, and how deploy windows/maintenance suppressions are handled.
Dashboard inventory and screenshots/links: per-model/regional panels, heatmaps, deploy annotations, and quick filters for GPU SKU/runtime build.
Alerting policy: thresholds, paging vs ticketing, alert grouping/dedup, maintenance windows, and oncall routing between Runtime and SRE.
Runbook for responders: confirm signal quality, compare slices (GPU/region/runtime), check recent deploys, capture profiler traces, mitigation/rollback steps.
Profiling playbook addendum tailored for canary regressions: recommended flags, kernel selection dumps, scheduler queue metrics, and common failure patterns.
Product/Console spec for how perf regression signals appear internally (and potential future customer-facing surfacing): UX requirements and API needs.
Release notes entry describing new runtime instrumentation hooks required by the canary (version tags, scheduler mode labels, kernel choice exports).
Initiative ticket: “Perf regression canary in prod” with milestones, owners, and links to design docs; parent for the workstream.
Define canary workload matrix (models, prompt shapes, streaming vs non-streaming, max tokens) and success criteria for stability/noise.
Implement canary runner service skeleton (config, scheduling loop, rate limiting, auth/credentials) and deployment plan.
Runtime instrumentation: emit scheduler mode, batch stats, KV cache metrics, and runtime build identifiers for canary requests.
Metrics definitions + aggregation pipeline changes for p95 and tokens/sec; ensure label schema aligns with cardinality budget.
Regression detector logic: baseline selection, drift handling, minimum sample size, deploy-window suppression, and alert payload fields.
Dashboards: per-model/regional views with deploy annotations and filters for GPU SKU; add links to runbook and recent PRs.
Alert routing: page SRE for initial triage, auto-assign Runtime when confirmed; define severity mapping and dedup keys.
Add runbook + training for oncall rotations; include ‘false positive’ playbook and how to file follow-up tuning tasks.
Rollout phase 1: enable in us-east for 2–3 models; monitor overhead and tune thresholds.
Rollout phase 2: expand to eu-west + additional models; validate GPU SKU slice correctness.
Noise reduction: warmup handling, cache priming strategy, and outlier filtering (e.g., node-level contention) without hiding real regressions.
Integrate incident-bot annotations: when a perf regression alert fires, auto-post to #eng-oncall with dashboards and deploy diffs.
Kernel/scheduling-specific slice: ensure canary can pin scheduler settings to reduce variance and isolate regressions.
Backtesting: replay historical metrics to estimate alert volume and adjust thresholds to avoid paging storms.
Security/privacy review: ensure canary prompts contain no customer data; confirm logs/metrics retention and access controls.
Operational readiness checklist: deploy rollback plan, ownership handoff, SLAs for alert response, and maintenance window guidelines.
Post-launch retro: what alerts were useful vs noisy, changes needed to detectors, and backlog for v2 (more workloads, better bisect hints).
PR: Add request-scoped tags for canary traffic (source=perf-canary) and propagate runtime_build + scheduler_mode through metrics/tracing.
PR: Emit batch composition stats (prefill/decode counts, max seq len) for canary requests; includes unit tests and metric naming review.
PR: Add kernel-selection debug export (selected kernel id + fallback reason) gated behind canary tag to control overhead.
PR: Fix tokens/sec calculation bug for streaming responses (alignment on first-token timestamp) discovered during canary prototyping.
PR: Add scheduler config pinning for canary runs (disable experimental heuristic X) to reduce variance and improve regression attribution.
PR: Add deploy annotation events to metrics (runtime_version, git_sha) for correlation in perf-canary dashboards.
PR: Introduce ‘canary-safe’ request class with strict rate limits and priority controls to avoid impacting customer queues.
PR: Add integration tests validating metric label schema/cardinality for canary dimensions (model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build).
PR: Optimize metric emission path to reduce overhead from high-frequency canary sampling; includes perf profiling notes.
PR: Hotfix: correct p95 aggregation window mismatch between runtime and telemetry pipeline; triggered by canary false positive.
PR: Initial perf-canary runner implementation (config, model list, prompt set loader, streaming/non-streaming modes).
PR: Add baseline computation + regression detector (rolling median, minimum sample size, deploy-window suppression).
PR: Add regional scheduler + GPU SKU awareness (tagging + routing); includes config examples for us-east/eu-west.
PR: Add alert payload enrichment (links to dashboards, last deploy, runtime build diff) and integration with incident-bot webhook.
PR: Reduce variance via warmup + cache priming steps; documents trade-offs and adds a ‘noise budget’ report.
PR: New Grafana dashboard JSON for perf-canary: per-model p95 + tokens/sec panels, annotations, and drill-down links.
PR: Alert rule definitions for perf regression detectors with dedup keys and severity mapping; includes review from SRE.
PR: Post perf-canary regression alerts to #eng-oncall with structured context fields and runbook links.
PR: Add helper for “regression vs baseline” alert semantics and maintenance-window suppression used by perf-canary.
PR: Export offline benchmark summary in a format comparable to prod canary slices (for sanity checks and drift investigations).

Transcript of a cross-team internal sync (recorded): Runtime + SRE + Telemetry review baseline strategy, rollout plan, and alert payload fields.
